newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore April oil exports fell 10.1-pct on year.
newsitem.headline: Singapore April oil exports fell 10.1-pct on year.

text.p: The value of Singapore's nominal domestic oil exports fell 10.1 percent in April from a year earlier to Singapore $1.314 million, the Trade Development Board (TDB) said on Tuesday.
"As in previous months, this was due to the softening of oil prices as well as a drop in volume due to the lacklustre demand from Malaysia and Thailand," the TDB said.
The data showed that exports rose 1.5 percent in April from March, when exports were valued at $1.294 billion.
The Ministry of Trade and Industry said on Friday that Singapore oil refineries were expected to be bearish on the oil market for the next six months, anticipating lower refining profit margins.
"Local refineries expect to see a decline in fuel margins with regional refineries returning from maintenance shutdowns by the third quarter of 1997," it said in a statement.
